items.method: Cross-read the market-heatmap breadth percentage against its 60% threshold and against the benchmark's distance from its 52-week high and its moving-average stack, then overlay the intraday session type and VWAP, the option-flow premium lean and single most-unusual print, and the VIX band, to judge whether an index still near its high is being confirmed by broad participation or has quietly narrowed while the tape sells and hedges at the margin.
items.note: Price is still near the high but participation underneath it has thinned sharply this window. SPY last printed 762.6, about 1.96% under its 52-week high, in a bull-stacked moving-average regime (50-day distance +1.55%, 200-day +7.84%, 126-day momentum +11.41%) — yet only 29.37% of the 134 market-heatmap constituents are positive on the day, a 30.63-point shortfall below the 60% broad-participation line, so leadership is narrow rather than broad. Underneath that, the session is a trend-day-down auction under mixed control with VWAP 764.84 above spot, and option premium is put-heavy across 12 tickers with 1940 contracts clearing the $250k bar inside 30 days; the single most-unusual print is an AVGO 420 put at $46.2M on 8.2x its open interest, a concentrated single-name downside bet. So a near-the-high index is being carried by a shrinking cohort while the intraday auction and the premium tape lean defensive. VIX 16.01 keeps this in a calm band. What to watch is whether breadth recovers back above the 60% line and premium rotates toward calls to confirm, or the trend-day-down drags price toward the lower option walls, with a daily close below 760.00 marking the point where the narrow-breadth top starts to resolve down.
items.title: SPY holds about 2% under its 52-week high while daily breadth has narrowed to 29.4% of constituents positive — a 30-point shortfall under the 60% line — with a trend-day-down tape and a concentrated AVGO put hedge

inputs: options-structure-lab.regime=negative dealer gamma; flip=766.85; callWall=765; putWall=760; expectedMove=3.65; spot=762.6
items.method: Read the options-structure gamma sign with its flip and wall levels against current benchmark spot, size the expected-move band around spot, confirm the dealer scenario and conviction from the gamma playbook, then overlay the intraday session type and VWAP and the VIX band, to judge whether short-gamma dealers are positioned to accelerate a break of the nearer wall or whether the corridor holds.
items.note: Dealer positioning and price sit in a short-gamma corridor with the walls straddling spot this window. Signed dealer gamma is negative, and SPY near 762.6 is below the 766.85 flip, wedged between a 765 call wall just overhead and a 760 put wall below. The front expected move is plus or minus 3.65, so the modelled band runs roughly 758.95 to 766.25 and both walls sit inside it, right where the trend-day-down auction under mixed control (VWAP 764.84 above spot) is pressing. Under negative gamma dealers hedge in the direction of the move, so sustained pressure toward the nearer 760 wall tends to extend rather than mean-revert. The gamma playbook reads range-break-watch with patient conviction. This is a coiled structure leaning down: while 760 holds and VIX 16.01 stays calm it can stay orderly, but a sustained daily close below the 760.00 put wall in short gamma is what tips the balance toward downside acceleration, whereas a clean reclaim of the 766.85 flip relieves the corridor to the upside.
items.title: SPY spot near 762.6 sits below the 766.85 negative-gamma flip and between a 765 call wall and a 760 put wall the intraday trend-day-down is pressing against

items.method: Cross-read the real-assets per-vehicle scores and the 63-day driver block (crypto and industrial/energy equity proxies versus gold, broad commodities and the gold/silver ratio) against the equity sector rotation and the benchmark regime, to judge whether the real-asset bid is risk-appetite-and-cyclical-led or monetary, and whether it agrees with where equity leadership is rotating.
items.note: The real-asset bid and the equity rotation disagree on risk appetite this window. Within real assets, crypto leads — ETH-USD at 71.1/100 and BTC-USD 66.5 in uptrends — while broad commodities DBC 62.6 and PDBC 62.6 and industrial copper CPER 59.3 hold firm, and the monetary metals lag: gold GLD reads 46.3 and mixed while silver SLV 22.2 is weak; IBIT 50 and oil USO 47.9 are mixed; 14 vehicles scored on a swing horizon. The 63-day driver block corroborates the risk-on, cyclical tilt: the bitcoin proxy runs +15.77 and the energy and industrial equity proxies +6.61 and +5.29 against a gold proxy of only -0.51 and a broad-commodity proxy of +0.74, and the gold-versus-silver ratio proxy is +10.89, meaning gold is outpacing silver. Yet the equity sector rotation reads the other way defensively — into XLU (Improving, accel +4.69), out of XLF (Weakening), with XLV (healthcare) Leading. So the real-asset complex leans risk-on through crypto and cyclicals while equity leadership leans defensive; the tension is whether the crypto-and-cyclical strength persists or converges down to the cautious equity read. VIX 16.01 is calm but the benchmark has slipped to about 2% under its high on a trend-day-down, so this rotation-quality divergence bears watching for which side resolves.
items.title: Real-asset leadership is crypto (ETH-USD 71.1, BTC-USD 66.5) and cyclical commodities (DBC 62.6, CPER 59.3) over monetary gold (GLD 46.3) and silver (SLV 22.2) while equity sector rotation turns defensive into XLU with XLV leading
